# Appeal of Denial — Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE: Request for Reconsideration of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Riley Foster
**Member ID:** W204716433
**Plan:** Banner Health (Commercial/ACA), Arizona
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-22
**Reference number:** POC-D5606CAED3-36942
**Governing policy cited by plan:** eviCore CMM-315 Shoulder Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures (https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-02/EviCore_CMM-315%20Shoulder%20Surg%20Arthro_Final_V1.0.2025_Pub02.25.2025.pdf)

Dear Banner Health Appeals Department,

I am writing to ask for reconsideration of the denial of my rotator cuff repair surgery (CPT 29827), referenced above. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking that this decision be reviewed again.

## Why I am appealing

My denial notice states that the reason for the determination is that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

I want to be transparent with the reviewer of this letter: the policy excerpts available to me from eviCore CMM-315 address criteria for labral repair, biceps tenodesis, shoulder instability/laxity procedures, and arthroscopic capsular release/manipulation under anesthesia. I have not been given the specific section of this policy that lists the medical necessity criteria for **rotator cuff repair**, and I am not able to quote language that was not provided to me. I am asking Banner Health to review my case against the rotator cuff repair criteria in its own CMM-315 policy, and to explain in writing which specific criterion or criteria my records are said to fail.

## What my records show

Based on the clinical summary submitted with my prior authorization request:

- **Duration and course of symptoms:** I have had 18 months of progressive shoulder pain that has not been relieved by rest.
- **Imaging:** An MRI of my shoulder on 2026-07-06 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:**
  - Supervised physical therapy for rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 10 weeks, 24 visits, from 2026-04-17 to 2026-06-26, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
  - NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief.
  - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-21, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Functional limitation:** I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height, and I cannot sleep on the affected side.
- **Physical exam:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **Other health factors:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

These records show an MRI-confirmed full-thickness rotator cuff tear, months of supervised physical therapy that did not resolve the problem, medication and injection treatment that did not provide lasting relief, and a clear functional impact on my daily life. My surgeon has reviewed this history and has documented that surgery is needed.

## What I am asking

I am asking Banner Health to:

1. Reconsider the denial of CPT 29827 in light of the imaging, conservative treatment history, and functional limitations described above; and
2. Identify, in writing, the specific medical necessity criteria from CMM-315 for rotator cuff repair that the plan believes my records do not meet, so that my surgeon and I can respond directly to that concern.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-18** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is unclear, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please let me know if any additional records are needed from my surgeon's office to complete this review. Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Riley Foster
Member ID: W204716433
Date: [date signed]
Contact phone: [phone number]
Contact address: [mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

 O’ Brien’s test  Biceps load test  Clunk test  Anterior slide test  Compression rotation test  Speed’s test  Modified dynamic labral shear  Function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment)  Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration  Other potential pathological cond itions have been excluded including, but not limited to, the following:

fracture, thoracic outlet syndrome, brachial plexus disorders, referred neck pain, cervical radiculopathy, a nd advanced glenohumeral osteoarthritis Labral Repair Non-Indic ations Not Medically Necessary  Labral repair is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition.
